title: Pima County Library Explains Delays in New Print Book Arrivals Due to Supplier Closure - NewsBreak
text:
3 hours ago In October 2025, the Pima County Public Library announced delays in receiving new print books. The delays are due to the closure of Baker & Taylor, a major U.S. book supplier. Baker & Taylor supplied books to schools, bookstores, and libraries, including Pima County.
The closure means library staff now handle tasks that Baker & Taylor employees previously managed. This has changed how the library acquires print books.
Some patrons have asked why the library does not order from Amazon. The library explained that Baker & Taylor supplied many titles to Amazon. Amazon cannot meet the large volume needs of libraries. The delay only affects print books. eBooks and audiobooks are still available through other vendors.
The library is working to sign a larger contract with Ingram Books, another distributor. The agreement is expected to be completed within a month. After that, the library will focus on filling existing holds and buying more copies to meet demand.
The library expects normal service to return by February 2026. Staff are working to reduce delays and maintain access to digital and print materials. The library thanks the community for its patience during this period.
